# `js/consistent-function-style`

**Functions take the syntax their role asks for**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `default`, `defaultExport`, `namedFunctions`, `namedExports`, `callbacks`, `objectProperties`, `reassignedVariables`, `typedVariables` |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (converting a callback between a function expression and an arrow changes `this` and `arguments` when the body uses them; only a callback whose body uses neither is offered, and the reviewer confirms) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-unicorn/consistent-function-style` |

## What it checks

Each role a function can have has a style the project may fix: `declaration` (`function f() {}`), `function-expression`, `arrow-function` or, for an object property, `method`; `ignore` (the default for every role) leaves it alone. The roles, in the order they are decided: a default export, a variable with a type annotation, a variable that is reassigned, a named export, a callback, an object property, a declared or variable function, and any other function. A function that is a class member, a parameter default or called on the spot is not read, and a generator is never asked to be an arrow. Behaviour of eslint-plugin-unicorn 79.0.0's rule, read and reimplemented. A finding offers the conversion only for a callback written as a function expression where an arrow is asked, or the reverse, and only when its body uses none of `this`, `arguments`, `super` or `new.target`, has no comment and has no type parameters; every other finding is reported without an edit.

Set the roles you care about: `[rules] "js/consistent-function-style" = { severity = "error", options = { namedFunctions = "declaration", callbacks = "arrow-function" } }`. With no `default`, `namedFunctions` or another role` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

**Why:** One syntax for one kind of function lets a reader tell a declared function from a callback at a glance.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | `string` | `""` | style of a function with no other role: declaration, function-expression, arrow-function or ignore |
| `defaultExport` | `string` | `""` | style of `export default function`; unset, an anonymous default export is not read |
| `namedFunctions` | `string` | `""` | style of a declared function or a `const f = …` function |
| `namedExports` | `string` | `""` | style of an exported function |
| `callbacks` | `string` | `""` | style of a function passed as an argument (function-expression, arrow-function or ignore) |
| `objectProperties` | `string` | `""` | style of a function that is an object property (method, function-expression, arrow-function or ignore) |
| `reassignedVariables` | `string` | `""` | style of a function assigned to a variable that is later reassigned |
| `typedVariables` | `string` | `""` | style of a function assigned to a variable with a type annotation |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
default = ""
defaultExport = ""
namedFunctions = ""
namedExports = ""
callbacks = ""
objectProperties = ""
reassignedVariables = ""
typedVariables = ""
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = { severity = "error", options = { default = "arrow-function", defaultExport = "<your value>", namedFunctions = "declaration", namedExports = "<your value>", callbacks = "arrow-function", objectProperties = "method", reassignedVariables = "function-expression", typedVariables = "<your value>" } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `default`

*string* · default `""`

style of a function with no other role: declaration, function-expression, arrow-function or ignore

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
default = "arrow-function"
```

#### `defaultExport`

*string* · default `""`

style of `export default function`; unset, an anonymous default export is not read

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
defaultExport = "<your value>"
```

#### `namedFunctions`

*string* · default `""`

style of a declared function or a `const f = …` function

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
namedFunctions = "declaration"
```

#### `namedExports`

*string* · default `""`

style of an exported function

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
namedExports = "<your value>"
```

#### `callbacks`

*string* · default `""`

style of a function passed as an argument (function-expression, arrow-function or ignore)

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
callbacks = "arrow-function"
```

#### `objectProperties`

*string* · default `""`

style of a function that is an object property (method, function-expression, arrow-function or ignore)

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
objectProperties = "method"
```

#### `reassignedVariables`

*string* · default `""`

style of a function assigned to a variable that is later reassigned

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
reassignedVariables = "function-expression"
```

#### `typedVariables`

*string* · default `""`

style of a function assigned to a variable with a type annotation

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
typedVariables = "<your value>"
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/consistent-function-style.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a named function as a declaration

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
namedFunctions = "declaration"
```

```js
const add = (a, b) => a + b;
function sub(a, b) {
  return a - b;
}
```

**Reports** at `1:13`.

#### a callback as an arrow, with a suggestion

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
callbacks = "arrow-function"
```

```js
items.map(function (x) {
  return x * 2;
});
```

**Reports** at `1:11`.

#### a callback that uses this has no suggestion

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
callbacks = "arrow-function"
```

```js
items.forEach(function (x) {
  this.add(x);
});
```

**Reports** at `1:15`.

#### a callback as a function expression

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
callbacks = "function-expression"
```

```js
items.map((x) => x * 2);
```

**Reports** at `1:11`.

#### object properties as methods

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
objectProperties = "method"
```

```js
const api = {
  run: () => 1,
  stop() {},
};
```

**Reports** at `2:8`.

#### a reassigned variable

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
reassignedVariables = "function-expression"
```

```js
let handler = () => 1;
handler = () => 2;
```

**Reports** at `1:15`.

#### a default export is read only when it is set

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
namedFunctions = "arrow-function"
```

```js
export default function () {}
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a generator is never asked to be an arrow

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
namedFunctions = "arrow-function"
```

```js
const gen = function* () {};
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a function called on the spot

```toml
[rules."js/consistent-function-style".options]
default = "arrow-function"
```

```js
(function () {})();
```

**Reports nothing.**

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/consistent-function-style" = { options = { default = "arrow-function" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/consistent-function-style" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/consistent-function-style" = { severity = "warn", options = { default = "arrow-function" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/consistent-function-style": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"default": "arrow-function"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/consistent-function-style: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/consistent-function-style expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/consistent-function-style --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/consistent-function-style       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/consistent-function-style  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## Examples

### JavaScript

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```js
items.map(function (x) {
  return x * 2;
});
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```js
items.map((x) => {
  return x * 2;
});
```

### JSX

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```jsx
items.map(function (x) {
  return x * 2;
});
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```jsx
items.map((x) => {
  return x * 2;
});
```

### TypeScript

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```ts
items.map(function (x) {
  return x * 2;
});
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```ts
items.map((x) => {
  return x * 2;
});
```

### TSX

#### Don't

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```tsx
items.map(function (x) {
  return x * 2;
});
```

#### Do

*With these options:* `{ callbacks = "arrow-function" }`

```tsx
items.map((x) => {
  return x * 2;
});
```
